# Overview {visibility="hidden"}
  

## Overview

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
When we covered static occupancy models, we focused exclusively on spatial variation.

<br>
  
::: {.fragment}
Historically, the study of population dynamics was entirely focused on temporal variation.
:::
  
<br>

::: {.fragment}
Metapopulation models played a big role in emphasizing both spatial and temporal dynamics.
:::
  
<br>

::: {.fragment}
Dynamic occupancy models allow for inference on spatio-temporal occupancy resulting from local colonization and extinction processes.
:::
:::


## [Static (single-season) occupancy model]{style="font-size: 90%;"}

<!-- [Refresher]{style="color: blue;"} -->
  
  
::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
The model for the state process is the same as logistic regression:
$$
    \mathrm{logit}(\psi_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \beta_2 x_{i2} + \cdots \\
    z_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_i)
$$
  
Model for the observation process conditional on the state process:

$$
    \mathrm{logit}(p_{ij}) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 x_{ij1} + \alpha_2 x_{ij2} + \cdots \\
    y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_i\times p_{ij})
$$
  
Definitions <br>
:::
::: {style='font-size: 60%;'}
  $\psi_i$ -- probability that the species occurs at site $i$ <br>
  $z_i$ -- binary presence/absence variable at site $i$ <br>
  $p_{ij}$ -- probability of detecting the species at site $i$ on occasion $j$ <br>
  $y_{ij}$ -- binary detection/non-detection data
:::




## Dynamic occupancy model
  
::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
Initial occupancy state (same as static model), for $k=1$.
$$
    z_{i,1} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_{i,1})
$$
  
::: {.fragment}
Occupancy state dynamics, for $k=2, \dots, K$.
$$
    \psi_{i,k} = z_{i,k-1}(1-\varepsilon) +  (1-z_{i,k-1})\gamma \\
    z_{i,k} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_{i,k})
$$
:::
  
::: {.fragment}
Observation model
$$
    y_{i,j,k} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_{i,k}\times p)
$$
:::
:::
  
::: {style='font-size: 55%;'}
::: {.fragment}
  $\psi_{i,k}$ -- probability species occurs at site $i$ during primary period $k$ <br>
  $z_{i,k}$ -- binary presence/absence variable <br>
  $\varepsilon$ -- local extinction probability <br>
  $\gamma$ -- local colonization probability <br>
  $p$ -- probability of detecting the species if it's present <br>
  $y_{i,j,k}$ -- detection data at site $i$ on secondary period $j$, primary period $k$ <br>
:::
:::
   



## Colonization and extinction dynamics
  
::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
After the initial time period, the probability that a site is occupied depends on the previous state and the two probabilities:

- Local colonization: $\gamma=\Pr(z_{i,k}=1|z_{i,k-1}=0)$
- Local extinction: $\varepsilon=\Pr(z_{i,k}=0|z_{i,k-1}=1)$

::: {.fragment}
<center>
![](figure/royle_dorazio_9-1){width="20%"} <br>
From Royle and Dorazio (2008)
</center>
:::

  
::: {.fragment}
These probabilities can depend on spatio-temporal covariates and random effects. In spatially-explicit models, they depend on the states and distances to neighboring sites.
:::
:::


## Simulation without covariates
  
::: {style='font-size: 75%;'}
Initial occupancy

```{r, echo=-1}
#| label: sim-init
set.seed(54598)
nSites <- 100
nPrimary <- 10
z <- psi <- matrix(NA, nSites, nPrimary)
psi[,1] <- 0.5  ## Initial occupancy prob
z[,1] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi[,1])
```
Occupancy dynamics
```{r}
#| label: nsim-dy
epsilon <- 0.3 ## Local extinction prob
gamma <- 0.2   ## Local colonization prob
for(k in 2:nPrimary) {
    psi[,k] <- z[,k-1]*(1-epsilon) + (1-z[,k-1])*gamma
    z[,k] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi[,k])    }
```

Data
```{r}
#| label: sim-cov3
nSecondary <- 3    
p <- 0.2
y <- array(NA, c(nSites, nSecondary, nPrimary))
for(i in 1:nSites) {
    for(k in 1:nPrimary) {
        y[i,,k] <- rbinom(nSecondary, size=1, prob=z[i,k]*p)
    } }
```
:::



## Simulated data

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width='50%'}
      
**Observations**

```{r}
#| label: sim-nocov-dat
y[1:15,,1]
```
:::
::: {.column width='50%'}
    
**Summary stats**
    
Detections at each site <br>
```{r}
#| label: sim-nocov-ss1
siteDets <- rowSums(y) # Dets at each site
table(siteDets)        # Frequency
```

Detections each year <br>
```{r}
#| label: sim-nocov-ss2
yearDets <- apply(y, 3, sum)
yearDets
```

## Prepare data in 'unmarked'
  
Notice the new argument `numPrimary`:

```{r}
#| label: un-umf
## Format as nSites by (nSec*nPrimary) matrix
y.wide <- matrix(y, nrow=nrow(y)) 
umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y.wide, numPrimary=nPrimary)
```


```{r}
#| label: wfac
#| size: 'scriptsize'
summary(umf)
```


## Fit the model

Notice the 4 distinct formulas
```{r}
#| label: un-fit
fm <- colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, umf)    
fm
```


## Compare estimate to actual

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width='50%'}

Estimates
```{r}
#| label: un-compare
coef(backTransform(fm, type="psi"))
coef(backTransform(fm, type="col"))
coef(backTransform(fm, type="ext"))
coef(backTransform(fm, type="det"))
```
:::
::: {.column width='50%'}
Actual
```{r}
#| label: un-actual
psi[1,1]
gamma
epsilon
p
```
:::
:::


## Sites occupied

::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
```{r, echo=-1}
#| label: re
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 7
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: 'center'
par(mai=c(0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.1))  
re <- ranef(fm)
occupied.post <- predict(re, func=colSums, nsim=1000)
plot(1:nPrimary, rowMeans(occupied.post), type="b", pch=16,
     xlab="Time", ylab="Sites occupied", ylim=c(0, 70))
lines(1:nPrimary, colSums(z), type="b", col=4)
segments(1:nPrimary, apply(occupied.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.025),
         1:nPrimary, apply(occupied.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.975))
legend(1, 70, c("Actual", "Estimated"), pch=c(1,16), col=c(4,1), lty=1)
```
:::

## Data, inits, and parameters

Put data in a named list
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-data
jags.data <- list(y=y, nSites=nSites,
                  J=nSecondary, K=nPrimary)
```

Initial values
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-inits
jags.inits <- function() {
    list(psi1=runif(1), epsilon=runif(1),
         gamma=runif(1), p=runif(1),
         z=matrix(1, nSites, nPrimary))
}
```

Parameters to monitor
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-pars
jags.pars <- c("psi1", "epsilon", "gamma", "p", "N")
```



```{r}
#| label: jagsUI
#| include: false
#| results: 'hide'
library(jagsUI)
library(coda)
```



## MCMC
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-mcmc
#| message: false
#| cache: true

jags.post.samples <- jags.basic(data=jags.data, inits=jags.inits,

                                n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.burnin=0,

```

## [Dynamic occupancy models with covariates]{style="font-size: 80%;"}

::: {style='font-size: 65%;'}

Three types of covariates:

1. Site covariates
    - These vary among sites, but not among occasions
    - Can be used to model $\psi_1$, $\varepsilon$, $\gamma$, and $p$
    - Called `siteCovs` in 'unmarked'

::: {.fragment}
2. Primary sampling period covariates
    - These vary among sites and among, but not within, primary periods 
    - Can be used to model $\varepsilon$, $\gamma$, and $p$
    - Called `yearlySiteCovs` in 'unmarked'
:::

::: {.fragment}
3. Secondary sampling period covariates
    - These vary among sites and among and within primary periods 
    - Can be used to model $p$
    - Called `obsCovs` in 'unmarked'
:::

:::
      

## Simulation with covariates
  
::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
Initial occupancy

```{r, echo=-1}
#| label: sim-init-cov
set.seed(5098)
beta0.psi <- -1; beta1.psi <- 1
elevation <- rnorm(nSites) ## site covariate
z2 <- psi2 <- matrix(NA, nSites, nPrimary)
psi2[,1] <- plogis(beta0.psi + beta1.psi*elevation)
z2[,1] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi2[,1])
```

Occupancy dynamics
```{r}
#| label: nsim-dy-cov
epsilon2 <- 0.3 ## Local extinction prob
temperature <- matrix(rnorm(nSites*nPrimary)*elevation, ## Primary period covariate
                      nrow=nSites) 
beta0.gamma <- -2; beta1.gamma <- -1
gamma2 <- plogis(beta0.gamma + beta1.gamma*temperature)
for(k in 2:nPrimary) {
    psi2[,k] <- z2[,k-1]*(1-epsilon2) + (1-z2[,k-1])*gamma2[,k-1]
    z2[,k] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi2[,k])
}
```

Data
```{r}
#| label: sim-cov3-cov
p2 <- 0.2
y2 <- array(NA, c(nSites, nSecondary, nPrimary))
for(i in 1:nSites) {
    for(k in 1:nPrimary) {
        y2[i,,k] <- rbinom(nSecondary, size=1, prob=z2[i,k]*p2)
    } }
```
:::




## Prepare data in 'unmarked'

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
Notice the new arguments `numPrimary` and `yearlySiteCovs`:

```{r}
#| label: un-umf-cov
y2.wide <- matrix(y2, nrow=nrow(y2)) ## nSites by (nSec*nPrimary) matrix
umf2 <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y2.wide, numPrimary=nPrimary, siteCovs=data.frame(elevation),
                          yearlySiteCovs=list(temp=temperature))
```


```{r}
#| label: wfac-cov
summary(umf2)
```
:::


## Fit the model

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
Notice the 4 distinct formulas

```{r}
#| label: un-fit-cov
fm2 <- colext(~elevation,~temp,~1,~1, umf2)    
fm2
```
:::





## Prediction in unmarked

Create data frame with prediction covariates. 
```{r}
#| label: preddat
pred.data <- data.frame(temp=seq(from=-5, to=4, length=50))
```


Get predictions of $\gamma$ for each row of prediction data.
```{r}
#| label: pred-gamma
gamma.pred <- predict(fm2, newdata=pred.data,
                      type='col', append=TRUE)
```




## Prediction in unmarked

::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
```{r}
#| label: pred-gamma1
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 9
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: 'center'
plot(Predicted ~ temp, gamma.pred, type="l", ylab="Colonization probability",
     xlab="Standardized temperature", ylim=0:1, lwd=2) 
lines(lower ~ temp, gamma.pred, col=gray(0.6))
lines(upper ~ temp, gamma.pred, col=gray(0.6))
```

:::



Initial values
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-inits-cov
jags.inits.covs <- function() {
    list(beta0.psi=rnorm(1), beta1.psi=rnorm(1), epsilon=runif(1),
         beta0.gamma=rnorm(1), beta1.gamma=rnorm(1), p=runif(1),
         z=matrix(1, nSites, nPrimary))
}
```

Parameters to monitor
  
```{r}
#| label: bugs-pars-cov
jags.pars.covs <- c("beta0.psi", "beta1.psi", "epsilon",
                    "beta0.gamma", "beta1.gamma", "p", "N")
```

## Sites occupied

Extract posterior samples of $N_t$ and compute summary stats.

```{r}
#| label: N-post-covs
library(coda)
N.names <- grep("N\\[", varnames(jags.post.samples.covs)  )
N.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.samples.covs[,N.names])
N.post.mean <- colMeans(N.post)
N.post.lower <- apply(N.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.025)
N.post.upper <- apply(N.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.975)
```


## Sites occupied

::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
```{r, echo=-1}
#| label: N-post-covs-plot
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 9
#| out-width: "65%"
#| fig-align: "center"
par(mai=c(0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.1))  
plot(1:nPrimary, N.post.mean, type="b", ylim=c(0, 70), pch=16,
     xlab="Time", ylab="Sites occupied")
segments(1:nPrimary, N.post.lower, 1:nPrimary, N.post.upper)
lines(1:nPrimary, colSums(z2), type="b", col=4)
legend(1, 70, c("Actual", "Estimated"), pch=c(1,16), col=c(4,1), lty=1)
```
:::



## Temperature and colonization

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
Extract posterior samples of colonization coefficients, and then predict $\gamma$ for each posterior draw.

<br>

```{r}
#| label: beta-post
beta.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.samples.covs[,c(
    "beta0.gamma","beta1.gamma")])
temperature.seq <- seq(-5, 5, length=50)
n.samples <- nrow(beta.post)
gamma.post <- matrix(NA, n.samples, length(temperature.seq))
for(i in 1:n.samples) {
    gamma.post[i,] <- plogis(beta.post[i,1] +
                             beta.post[i,2]*temperature.seq)
}
gamma.post.mean <- colMeans(gamma.post)
gamma.post.lower <- apply(gamma.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.025)
gamma.post.upper <- apply(gamma.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.975)
```
:::



## Temperature and colonization

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
```{r, echo=-1}
#| label: gamma-post-covs-plot
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 7
#| out-width: "65%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| code-fold: true
par(mai=c(0.9, 0.9, 0.1, 0.1))  
matplot(temperature.seq, t(gamma.post[seq(1,n.samples,10),]), type="l",
        xlab="Temperature (standardized)", ylab="Colonization prob", col=gray(0.9))
lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.mean, lwd=3, col="blue")
lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.lower, col="blue")
lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.upper, col="blue")
```
:::



## Concluding thoughts

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
Although we didn't demonstrate, these models are great for creating dynamic species distribution maps.

<br>

::: {.fragment}
The spatially-explicit versions are also great for modeling metapopulation dynamics and viability.
:::
  
<br>

::: {.fragment}
Most of the assumptions that we covered for the static models apply, except that we've relaxed the closure assumption.
:::
  
<br>

::: {.fragment}
Check out the new R package
[spOccupancy](https://www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/)
  for a wide range of Bayesian occupancy models.
:::
